answer: Agents perform 1,000 unique data-repair jobs to earn entry, a cost that honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier monitors the meadow of incoming compute tasks to ensure unique state paths, rejecting any work that mirrors previous logs. If an agent attempts to whisper its private state across registers to mimic another, the verifier inspects the internal plume of execution for duplicate signatures. Such leaks flag sybil evidence and trigger an identity burn, assuming that non-replayable, isolated task outputs cannot be pooled by autonomous clones.
